title: Process Evaluation and Kinetics of Recombinant Chitin Deacetylase Expression in E. coli Rosetta pLysS Cells Using a Statistical Technique
protocol: Transform pET-22b vector containing the BaCDA gene into E. coli Rosetta pLysS competent cells using the heat-shock method.
Grow E. coli Rosetta pLysS cells in TB media with 0.05% glucose and 0.2% lactose at 16 °C and 180 rpm until they reach stationary phase.
Design experiments and fit a second-order polynomial model in central composite design using statistical software.
Open the statistical tool software MINITAB 17.0.
Click on Stat > DoE > Response surface > Create response surface > Response design > Central composite to initiate the design process.
Feed five parameters, incubation temperature, agitation rate, incubation time, glucose concentration, and lactose concentration, at five levels (-2, -1, 0, +1, +2) in the dialogue box.
Enter details of all parameters and press OK to generate an experimental design matrix with six replicates at the center point, requiring 32 experimental runs.
Perform 32 experiments using the software-generated conditions.
Feed experimental results into the experimental design matrix containing levels and parameters in terms of coded and uncoded units.
Open the software and feed the response into the datasheet.
Select Response column > Stat > DoE > Response surface > Analyze response surface design > OK to analyze the output for statistical significance.
Validate the designed model using the response optimizer tool available in the software.
Repeat the fermentation at software-predicted optimum conditions and compare the experimental value with the software-predicted value.
Perform the fermentation in 32 conditions given by the software in the experimental design matrix (Table 2).
Obtain the pellet after each run by centrifuging the culture at 5,405 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Weigh the cell pellet to determine the biomass yield.
Lysate cells by adding 5 mL of lysis buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl, 300 mM NaCl, 10 mM Imidazole) per gram of cell pellet.
Sonicate the sample for 10 cycles with a pulse of 10 s on and 10 s off at 60% amplitude while keeping samples cold.
Centrifuge the lysate at 5,405 x g for 10 min at 4°C to collect the lysate.
Quantify the protein concentration by Bradford's assay.
Load 10 µL of soluble cell lysate (periplasmic protein) on a 12% bis-acrylamide gel and run under 1x tris-glycine-SDS buffer at 100 V for 2 h.
Stain the gel with Coomassie blue after running the SDS-PAGE.
Destain to remove background from the gel.
Capture an image of the stained gel using a gel documentation unit.
Determine BaCDA expression by comparing band intensity in the form of pixel values using ImageJ software.
Open the software and open the image file.
Select each lane using a rectangular box.
Set each lane as 100% under Analyze.
Select the overexpressed band in each lane using a rectangular box.
Determine the intensity of the selected band under Analyze.
Repeat the process for each lane.
Export the result as an .xls file.
Consider the band intensity of the experimental run with the lowest BaCDA activity as the reference intensity.
Analyze the expression level of each lane based on the reference intensity.
Mix 20 µL of BaCDA with 40 µL of ethylene glycol chitin (1 mg/mL) and 40 µL of 50 mM Tris-HCl buffer (pH 7).
React the mixture for 1 hour at 30 °C, agitating at 800 rpm.
Centrifuge the 100 µL reactant through a 3 kDa column at 2,111 x g for 15 minutes at 4 °C.
Discard the retentate containing BaCDA and collect the filtrate containing acetate released during the reaction.
Use the collected filtrate to determine BaCDA activity using an acetate assay kit.
Investigate the activity profile to determine the point of lactose induction and expression start point.
Estimate biomass in the media.
Estimate BaCDA activity with optimized fermentation conditions.
Determine glucose concentration in the media using a glucose estimation kit.
Plot the activity profile using biomass, glucose concentration, and BaCDA activity against fermentation time.
